local_verification_required: Windows installed app (coordinator, deferred): with a backed-up copy of a pre-PBK-26 Obsidian export folder, add your own quote and **Note:** line below the last highlight of one note and a line between two highlights of another; sync: first keeps every byte, second is listed under 'Not exported' and is unchanged; move the line to the end and sync: migrated.

Windows: Obsidian on Windows may save notes with CRLF; a fully CRLF note is never written (treated as not Properbooky's; a new note is written beside it) - confirm on a real vault whether Obsidian rewrites line endings.
review_walkthrough: Previous build: highlight two books, sync to Obsidian. In one note add your own text, a '> quote' and a '**Note:**' line at the end; in the other write a line between two highlights.
New build: Obsidian > Sync highlights now: the first note keeps everything you wrote below the new block; the second is listed under 'Not exported' with how to fix it and is untouched.
Move the line to the end of the second note, sync again: migrated, your text kept. Sync again / restart: '(0 updated)'.
known_risks: Design choice (conservative): a legacy entry is proven only with the blank line the old exporter wrote after it; text typed directly under a highlight is refused (no write) rather than migrated. Option for coordinator: accept a missing trailing blank line.
A legacy note whose old note text was later edited in the app keeps the old '**Note:** …' line as user text below the block (preserved, not deleted); in the middle of the note it causes a refusal.

Adjacent, pre-existing, NOT changed (escalated): when Properbooky's own frontmatter keys change (e.g. catalog title corrected), merge_frontmatter re-serializes the mapping and drops YAML comments/formatting of the user's other keys (values kept). Reproduced at cfb40a5 with a scratch probe.
Rollback limitation unchanged: the previous build regenerates notes wholesale if used to sync after a rollback.
